# Bhikkhu Saṁyutta (SN 21)
**ID:** SN 21
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Saṁyutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn21
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0302m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Comparative scholarship has examined the collection alongside its Chinese parallels in the *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ, T 99) and the *Bieyi za ahan jing* (SĀ², T 100), establishing that doctrinal differences between the versions are minimal and confined primarily to narrative or scholastic variations [Shulman 2014; Bingenheimer 2011]. Nine suttas have direct parallels in SĀ and seven in SĀ², with occasional parallels in the *Ekottarāgama* (EĀ), including alignments for the *Kolitasutta* (SĀ 501), the *Nandasutta* (EĀ 18.6, SĀ 1067, SĀ² 5), and the *Tissasutta* (SĀ 1068, SĀ² 7) [SuttaCentral; Bingenheimer 2011]. Automated text reuse analysis by DharmaNexus aligns segments of SN 21 with numerous internal Pali texts—most extensively the *Moggallāna Saṁyutta* (SN 40), the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), and parts of the *Aṅguttaranikāya*—as well as cross-language parallels in Chinese Āgamas (T 99, T 100, T 26, T 125), Sanskrit Vinaya fragments (*Saṅghabhedavastu*), and Tibetan Vinaya literature [DharmaNexus].

- This file contains 11 suttas; 11 of them have parallels listed on SuttaCentral. Full parallels by collection: SĀ (9), SA2 (7), Pali (2), EĀ (1)

**Sources**

- [SuttaCentral] SuttaCentral, Bhikkhusaṁyutta (sn21) record — Supplied title, blurb, sutta count, and curated Chinese/Pali parallel correspondences.
